t: Why Perspective uses its own data connection
x: Why Perspective uses its own data connection Perspective is a columnar analytics engine, not a conventional DOM table. Its websocket protocol moves table updates into a browser worker and supports views, aggregations, and incremental computation without serializing the full dataset through the component tree. spaday-perspective therefore separates two kinds of state: bulk rows travel through Perspective’s native websocket; connection URL, theme, and saved workspace layout remain ordinary serializable component properties. This boundary keeps Python authoring declarative while preserving Perspective’s high-performance data path. A spaday store or transports model can still carry compact application state, such as the selected layout preset or summary metrics. Sending every row through spaday would duplicate storage and serialization work before Perspective could process the same data again. Keeping the native connection also means existing Perspective server code can be used unchanged. The wrapper only adapts lifecycle, theme, and workspace configuration to spaday. x: Use showTable to select a table’s detail panel and update filters in one action: from spaday import Invoke, by_id, element element("button").text("Buy trades").on( "click", Invoke( by_id("workspace"), "showTable", "trades", {"filter": [["side", "==", "Buy"]]}, result="shown", ), ) Declare trades in config.panel_defaults or config.tables. If only a master panel shows the table, this opens a separate detail panel using the panel defaults. Existing filters on other columns remain; the action replaces only the side clauses. The result field contains the selected panel ID for later restorePanel or exportData actions.

s: Embed a grid without internal tabs
x: Set hide_tabs=True when your application already supplies navigation: panel = PerspectiveViewer( hide_tabs=True, config={ "ws_url": "/perspective", "workspace": { "panels": {"trades": {"table": "trades", "plugin": "Datagrid"}}, "layout": {"type": "tab-layout", "tabs": ["trades"]}, }, }, ).style(height="24rem", width="100%", min_width="0") Give the grid a definite height, including inside a WebAwesome tab panel. height="100%" needs a parent with a definite height; otherwise the grid can collapse. A sized grid observes its container when the tab becomes visible and when the container resizes. No tab-show callback is required. hide_tabs changes presentation only. For several tables, retain toolbar=True or supply buttons calling openTablePanel as shown above. The example uses the wrapper toolbar with hidden internal tabs.

x: Attach this action to your own button to download the configured view as CSV: from spaday import Download, Invoke, Sequence, by_id, field export_trades = Sequence( Invoke(by_id("workspace"), "exportData", {"panel": "trades", "format": "csv"}, result="exported_trades"), Download("trades.csv", field("exported_trades"), "text/csv"), ) Use format="json" in the options mapping for JSON text, or omit panel to export the active panel. x: Keep the table returned by client.table(), then update it whenever application data changes: trades = client.table(schema, limit=1_000, name="trades") trades.update( [ { "symbol": "NVDA", "quantity": 50, "price": 182.40, } ] ) Connected viewers receive the update through Perspective’s websocket. Do not copy bulk rows into a spaday store.

s: Add a delete button to each row
x: Create the source table with a unique index, include that column in the Datagrid, and annotate it: from spaday import CallEndpoint, event_prop, obj from spaday_perspective import PerspectiveViewer orders = client.table(rows, name="orders", index="id") panel = PerspectiveViewer( config=config, row_actions={"orders": {"id": {"action": "delete", "label": "Delete order"}}}, ).on( "perspective-row-action", CallEndpoint("POST", "/orders/delete", obj({"id": event_prop("detail.key")}), result="reply"), ) In the endpoint, validate the ID and the authenticated user’s permission, then update authoritative storage and call orders.remove([key]). Use reply to show success or rejection. Do not delete by displayed row number or use a clicked group’s filters as a bulk-delete predicate. If several actions share a handler, validate the requested action and table against an allowlist too. The main example (python -m spaday_perspective.example) and browser preview include delete buttons in the live blotter. Both call the same Python deletion handler. t: How to stream data and change layouts
x: Perspective uses its own theme names. Compute the wrapper property explicitly: from spaday import cond, field panel.compute("theme", cond(field("dark"), "dark", "light")) The aliases map to Pro Dark and Pro Light (spaday_perspective.THEMES). A full Perspective theme name is also accepted, so to use themes of your own, put their CSS on the page and compute their names instead: panel.compute("theme", cond(field("dark"), "Acme Dark", "Acme Light"))

s: Configure selection and find a value
x: Enable region selection, cell-aligned scrolling, and Find from Python: from spaday_perspective import EditMode, PerspectiveViewer, Theme panel = PerspectiveViewer( theme=Theme.DARK, toolbar=True, find=True, config={ "ws_url": "/perspective", "workspace": { "layout": {"type": "tab-layout", "tabs": ["trades"]}, "panels": { "trades": { "table": "trades", "plugin": "Datagrid", "plugin_config": {"edit_mode": EditMode.SELECT_REGION, "scroll_lock": True}, }, }, }, }, ) Select cells and press Ctrl+C / Cmd+C to copy. Press Ctrl+F / Cmd+F while the grid is focused, or click Find, then choose a column and enter an exact value. Apply filter keeps existing filters. Use Perspective Settings to change or remove them. Cancel leaves the data view unchanged. The main Python example and browser preview include these controls. To use a custom Find button, call Invoke(by_id("your-panel-id"), "openFind") from its click action; keep find=True on the panel.

x: perspective-config-update re-dispatches whenever the user edits the workspace — drags a panel, changes a view, filters. Save the whole workspace before sending it to your endpoint: from spaday import CallEndpoint, Invoke, Sequence, by_id, field panel.on( "perspective-config-update", Sequence( Invoke(by_id("workspace"), "saveWorkspace", result="saved_workspace"), CallEndpoint("POST", "/api/layout", field("saved_workspace")), ), ) Give the wrapper id="workspace". Serve the stored token back through config["workspace"] on the next load.

t: How to stream data and change layouts
s: Mirror a table into a local worker
x: For tables that are read-heavy in the browser, mirror them client-side with a per-table architecture — reads (scrolls, sorts, filters) stop round-tripping to Python: panel = PerspectiveViewer( config={ "ws_url": "/perspective", "tables": [ {"name": "trades", "architecture": "client-server", "index": "symbol"}, "orders", # plain entries stay on the server ], "workspace": layout, } ) index and limit apply to the local copy. default_architecture flips the default for every plain entry. Mirrors resnapshot after source changes so deletions and replacements propagate correctly. Keep large, high-frequency tables on the default server architecture to avoid full-table transfer on refresh.

s: Share Perspective with your own library
x: Perspective registers global custom element names, so a second copy on the page throws from customElements.define. If your library uses Perspective, import it by its bare specifiers and leave those imports out of your bundle: // esbuild await esbuild.build({ entryPoints: ["src/index.js"], bundle: true, format: "esm", external: [ "@perspective-dev/client", "@perspective-dev/viewer", "@perspective-dev/viewer-charts", "@perspective-dev/viewer-datagrid", ], }); Serve your bundle as a module next to packages=["perspective"]; the page’s import map resolves those imports to the copy this package already loaded. Import @perspective-dev/viewer dynamically — import("@perspective-dev/viewer") — rather than statically: it instantiates its WASM with a top-level await, so a static import holds back your whole module, and any element it defines, until the binary has loaded, and spaday can mount the page before your element exists. To share the engine itself rather than just the modules, borrow it: globalThis.__spadayPerspective.client(url) returns the websocket client the panels use for that server, and .worker() the shared local engine.

A table holds data. A view defines a query over a table. A panel displays a view in a workspace. A workspace contains the layout tree and panel configurations. The following legacy names remain supported: Canonical name Compatibility name PerspectiveViewer PerspectivePanel config.workspace config.layout config.panel_defaults config.channels config.restore_selected_tabs_only config.single_tab openTablePanel(name) openChannel(name) closeTablePanels(name) closeChannel(name) saveWorkspace() save() savePortableWorkspace() saveClean() Supplying both config names requires structurally equal values; conflicting values raise an error. The config getter preserves the supplied keys. Workspace JSON strings are accepted; when supplying both workspace aliases, their values must use the same representation. Canonical save methods write the wrapper extension retained_panel_configs_by_table. Legacy save methods keep writing closed_channels; restores accept either key and reject conflicting mappings. Both mappings store one last panel configuration per table, only for tables without open panels. The wrapper removes this metadata before calling native restoreWorkspace(). The public spaday_perspective.PerspectiveViewer validates literal configuration when serialized with to_node() (including through serve() or a widget). This includes .prop("config", ...) updates. validate_config(config) performs the same check explicitly and raises ValueError with a path such as config.workspace.panels.trades.plugin_config.edit_mode. Browser property setters validate reactive config updates before accepting them. Computed expressions are checked when their result reaches the browser, not while authoring the expression. Validation covers wrapper flags, table descriptors, panel defaults, theme-name types, and the pinned Datagrid’s plugin settings. Unknown Datagrid settings are rejected. Custom plugins, per-column style payloads, and table-dependent filter/expression validity remain upstream-owned. Unknown wrapper/workspace extension fields are preserved. This is not a complete validator for every Perspective plugin or layout tree. The shared Datagrid contract is checked against the installed plugin’s live settings schema and TypeScript enum declarations. An upstream field, type, or enum change fails those tests. Positive finite font sizes and row heights are accepted

A server table (the default) reads over the websocket: every scroll, sort, and filter round-trips to the Python server. A client-server table mirrors into a local Web Worker engine: the wrapper opens the server table and replaces a local copy (with the entry’s index / limit) from an Arrow snapshot after source changes, loading the worker client before the websocket client so the local copy wins the viewer’s table-name lookup. Reads are then local; the server stays authoritative for writes. Set architectures in the initial config — changing the mirrored set later reconnects. Row deltas omit deleted keys. Snapshot replacement propagates removals, clear, and replace operations and avoids duplicate appends for unindexed mirrors. Refreshes are serialized and notifications during an in-flight refresh coalesce into another snapshot. This sends the full source table on refresh; server architecture avoids that cost for large or frequently changing tables.

row_actions (JavaScript rowActions) maps table names to indexed-column button descriptions: PerspectiveViewer(row_actions={"orders": {"id": {"action": "delete", "label": "Delete order", "text": "×"}}}) A column accepts one description or a list, rendered in order in the same cell: PerspectiveViewer(row_actions={"orders": {"id": [ {"action": "delete", "label": "Delete order"}, {"action": "copy", "label": "Copy order to form", "text": "⧉"}, ]}}) Dedicated columns use identifiers starting with @ and do not replace the real index column: PerspectiveViewer(row_actions={"orders": { "@copy": { "header": "Copy", "position": "start", "buttons": [{"action": "copy", "label": "Copy order", "icon": "copy"}], }, "@delete": { "header": "Delete", "position": "end", "buttons": [{"action": "delete", "label": "Delete order", "icon": "delete"}], }, }}) Any number of dedicated columns may appear at either end, in mapping insertion order within each position. Each accepts multiple buttons. Headers must be unique and must not collide with source columns or user expressions. An empty button list removes the generated column. View-level expressions provide the record keys; source tables are unchanged. The

Perspective’s viewer events do not bubble, so the panel re-dispatches the observational set as bubbling DOM events usable from spaday’s .on(...): perspective-click, perspective-select, perspective-global-filter, perspective-global-filter-update, perspective-config-update, perspective-toggle-settings, perspective-statusbar-pointerdown, and perspective-table-delete. perspective-config-update fires on user edits (layout drags, view changes, filters). A handler can call saveWorkspace() to capture the whole workspace for persistence; the event payload is not a workspace token. Two wrapper lifecycle events complete the picture: perspective-ready fires once, after the panel has connected, loaded its tables, and applied and rendered its initial workspace config — the signal to dismiss a branded startup overlay — and perspective-error fires when a config apply fails (connection, mirror, or restore), with the error in detail, so a host can swap its loader for an error state. The cancelable *-before events are not re-dispatched; attach to the viewer directly for those.

exportData({panel?, format?}) returns CSV text by default or JSON text with format: "json". panel defaults to the active panel. It exports the configured view, excluding synthetic action value columns, and retains filtering, sorting, grouping, splitting and expressions. Group keys remain present, including when a generated expression is used as a grouping key. This exports the whole configured view rather than the selected block or viewport. The temporary export view is deleted on success and failure; the displayed view is not changed. Native Perspective export and selected-cell copying retain their original view-based behavior: selected/exported action fields contain record IDs. exportData provides the separate data-only path used by the example’s Export CSV button. openFind() opens the column/value prompt for the active panel when find=True. With the toolbar enabled, Find invokes this method. Ctrl+F / Cmd+F instead targets the Datagrid receiving the key event. Other page content, editable inputs, and wrappers with Find disabled keep browser find behavior. Find lists source-table columns and uses ==, converting the entered value to the column’s type. spaday_perspective.TOKENS lists spa_perspective_action_color, spa_perspective_action_background, and spa_perspective_action_border for the optional row buttons. Pass these keywords to .css() to set the corresponding --spa-perspective-* properties. spa_perspective_divider_color controls panel borders and resize gaps; spa_perspective_divider_hover_color controls feedback while hovering or dragging a divider. Defaults follow Perspective’s inactive border and active colors in light and dark themes. These do not replace Perspective’s grid themes. PerspectiveViewer().css( spa_perspective_divider_color="#666", spa_perspective_divider_hover_color="#0af", ) The wrapper contains frame and title overflow and uses Perspective’s own resize coordination. Applications do not need shadow-root observers or frame selectors. These frame styles target the pinned Perspective minor version and have narrow-pane and divider-drag tests in Chromium and WebKit. Legacy --psp-workspace--tabbar-* variables belong to the removed workspace component and do not style Perspective 5.6 frames. spaday_perspective.package is named perspective. Its browser asset defines <perspective-panel> and the Perspective themes, and loads Perspective’s own client, viewer, datagrid and charts modules, which the package serves under vendor/ beside their WASM binaries. Its components collection contains PerspectiveViewer; catalog returns the wrapper’s property, event, and slot schema. package.imports publishes those modules under Perspective’s bare specifiers, which spaday emits as the page’s import map: Specifier Served from @perspective-dev/client vendor/@perspective-dev/client/dist/cdn/perspective.js @perspective-dev/viewer vendor/@perspective-dev/viewer/dist/cdn/perspective-viewer.js @perspective-dev/viewer-charts vendor/@perspective-dev/viewer-charts/dist/cdn/perspective-viewer-charts.js @perspective-dev/viewer-datagrid vendor/@perspective-dev/viewer-datagrid/dist/cdn/perspective-viewer-datagrid.js Any other module on the page that imports them gets the same copy.

Config updates skip superseded work that has not started. An already-running upstream restore finishes before the newest config applies. Imperative methods remain queued in order. Saved workspaces with the same panel IDs, tables, plugins, and style settings reuse existing plugins, including inactive tabs. Only panels whose view configuration changed are restored; unchanged panels receive no per-panel restore. Comparison uses live state, so restoring a saved workspace resets user edits. Reuse requires complete saved configurations and unchanged derived tables. Incomplete configurations, added or removed panels, table/plugin/style changes, and row-action policies use a full restore. Perspective merges plugin and column styles during per-panel updates; full restoration preserves the replacement semantics of saved workspaces in those cases. js/tests/workspace-restores.spec.js measures layout-only changes on 48 panels and changed saved workspaces on 48 Datagrid panels over 100,000 synthetic trade rows. Build a live market workspace In this tutorial, you will serve a named Perspective table and display it in a spaday component tree. Install the packages pip install "spaday[examples]" spaday-perspective "perspective-python>=4.5,<4.6" Create the server and table Save this as market_app.py: import perspective import uvicorn from perspective.handlers.starlette import PerspectiveStarletteHandler from spaday.backends.starlette import serve from spaday_perspective import PerspectiveViewer from starlette.routing import WebSocketRoute from starlette.websockets import WebSocket server = perspective.Server() client = server.new_local_client() client.table( [ {"symbol": "AAPL", "quantity": 100, "price": 211.10}, {"symbol": "MSFT", "quantity": 75, "price": 503.02}, ], name="trades", ) async def perspective_socket(websocket: WebSocket) -> None: await PerspectiveStarletteHandler( perspective_server=server, websocket=websocket, ).run() Perspective owns this websocket and the bulk table data carried by it. Add the panel Continue in the same file: # Perspective's whole-element config: a regular-layout tree plus per-panel viewer configs layout = { "layout": {"type": "tab-layout", "tabs": ["market"]}

Save this as market_app.py: import perspective import uvicorn from perspective.handlers.starlette import PerspectiveStarletteHandler from spaday.backends.starlette import serve from spaday_perspective import PerspectiveViewer from starlette.routing import WebSocketRoute from starlette.websockets import WebSocket server = perspective.Server() client = server.new_local_client() client.table( [ {"symbol": "AAPL", "quantity": 100, "price": 211.10}, {"symbol": "MSFT", "quantity": 75, "price": 503.02}, ], name="trades", ) async def perspective_socket(websocket: WebSocket) -> None: await PerspectiveStarletteHandler( perspective_server=server, websocket=websocket, ).run() Perspective owns this websocket and the bulk table data carried by it.

Continue in the same file: # Perspective's whole-element config: a regular-layout tree plus per-panel viewer configs layout = { "layout": {"type": "tab-layout", "tabs": ["market"]}, "panels": { "market": { "table": "trades", "plugin": "Datagrid", "columns": ["symbol", "quantity", "price"], } }, } panel = PerspectiveViewer( config={ "ws_url": "/perspective", "tables": ["trades"], "workspace": layout, }, theme="light", style="height: 32rem", ) app = serve( panel, packages=["perspective"], routes=[WebSocketRoute("/perspective", perspective_socket)], ) if __name__ == "__main__": uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=8000) Run python market_app.py, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000. You should see both rows in a Perspective datagrid. You now have a live Perspective table and a serializable workspace configuration. This complete app serves a live Perspective table. Add trade streams a new row into the grid, the select switches between flat and grouped layouts, and the checkbox changes the viewer theme. import perspective from perspective.handlers.starlette import PerspectiveStarletteHandler from starlette.responses import JSONResponse from starlette.routing import Route, WebSocketRoute from starlette.websockets import WebSocket from spaday import CallEndpoint, cond, element, eq, field, obj from spaday.backends.starlette import serve from spaday_perspective import PerspectiveViewer server = perspective.Server() client = server.new_local_client() trades = client.table( [ {"id": 1, "symbol": "AAPL", "side": "buy", "price": 211.10}, {"id": 2, "symbol": "MSFT", "side": "sell", "price": 503.02}, ], name="trades", ) next_id = 2 async def add_trade(_request): global next_id next_id += 1 trades.update( [ { "id": next_id, "symbol": "AAPL" if next_id % 2 else "MSFT", "side": "buy" if next_id % 2 else "sell", "price": 210 + next_id, } ] ) return JSONResponse({"id": next_id}) async def perspective_socket(websocket: WebSocket): await PerspectiveStarletteHandler(perspective_server=server, websocket=websocke
